sources.entry: Pillager - macOS Video Downloader written in Swift and Objective-C.

summary.one_liner: Pillager is a macOS video downloader app written in Swift and Objective-C that fetches videos from web pages.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a macOS app that downloads videos from web pages, offering mp4, webm, flv, and mp3 (audio only) formats when available. It picks the best quality when several versions exist. Users can abort downloads and run more than one download at a time. Two unchecked roadmap items are an automatic queue limiting simultaneous downloads to three and the ability to stop and resume downloads later. The app relies on youtube-dl, which the README says is included in the package, and on an FFmpeg binary that the builder must add manually in Xcode.
use_cases: download videos from web pages on a mac
save web videos as mp4 or webm
extract audio from online videos as mp3
batch download several videos at once
how_to_run: Run `brew install ffmpeg` in the terminal
Run `brew --prefix ffmpeg` to find the FFmpeg install path
Drag the ffmpeg binary from the bin subdirectory into the "Exec" group in Xcode
notable: Pulls video downloads through youtube-dl, with youtube-dl bundled in the source package
FFmpeg is not shipped; the builder imports their own compiled binary to avoid license issues
Supports mp4, webm, flv, and mp3 audio-only output
caveats: macOS only, and building requires Xcode
Requires a manually imported FFmpeg binary before the app will build
Automatic download queue and pause/resume are listed as unfinished features
